Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd ratehr just be referred to as the claimant for this, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was stopped at a light on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, waiting to turn left.
Q: What happened next?
A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. The car behind me didn't stop in time and hit my rear bumper pretty solidly.
Q: Were you able to move your vehicle after the impact?
A: Yes, I pulled over to the shoulder. The car was drivable but the back end was crushed.
Q: Did you speak with the other driver?
A: Briefly. He said he looked down at his phone for a second and didn't see the light change to red in time.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: Yes, that evening. My neck was stiff, but the bigger problem is my right shoulder. It hurts when I lift anything above
my head.
Q: Have you been treated since then?
A: I've had two visits so far and I'm doing some physical therapy. The doctor said it could take several weeks to
improve.
Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: A few days, yes. My job involves a lot of lifting, so I've had to limit my duties.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?
A: Just that I've been careful about following the treatment plan, and I'm hoping to get back to normal soon.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
